note: Upstream pins keras==2.3.1 / tensorflow==2.0.1, which import keras.layers.recurrent and keras.layers.core -- module paths removed in later Keras. Neither pinned version has an arm64 macOS wheel. The arms are therefore run through a PORT that reproduces the upstream architecture, optimizer, loss, batch size, dropout, epoch cap, early-stopping patience and min_delta exactly as read from upstream config.yaml, on a modern TensorFlow. The port is identical between the two arms, so it cannot favour either; it is recorded here because it is a deviation from running upstream code verbatim.

amendment_1.what: The pre-registration declared that both arms would run through a PORT of upstream modeling.py, because upstream imports keras.layers.recurrent and keras.layers.core, module paths removed in later Keras.
amendment_1.finding: A port is not necessary. Registering two alias modules that re-export LSTM, Dense, Activation and Dropout from modern keras.layers makes upstream modeling.py, errors.py and detector.py all import VERBATIM. Verified by import.
amendment_1.effect: Strictly REDUCES deviation from upstream: the architecture, training loop, thresholding and scoring are now upstream's own code rather than a reimplementation. The arms, channel, seeds and endpoints are untouched.
amendment_1.why_recorded: The pre-registration promised to declare deviations in advance rather than discover them in results. Finding that a declared deviation is unnecessary is the same obligation running the other way.

amendment_2.what: Three version bridges were needed to run upstream code on current libraries. All three are in this study's own files; the upstream clone stays byte-identical and `git status` on it is empty, so the per-file sha256 in run_manifest.json still verify.
bridges: keras.layers.recurrent / keras.layers.core alias modules re-exporting LSTM, Dense, Activation, Dropout from modern keras.layers. Upstream imports those removed paths.

np.delete index cast. errors.py:407 creates i_to_remove as np.array([]) -- float64 -- and it stays float after np.append. numpy 1.17.4 (upstream's pin) accepted a float index array with a deprecation; numpy 2 raises. The values are always integral positions so the cast changes nothing. It applies ONLY when the array is floating AND every value is integral, so a genuinely fractional index still raises rather than being rounded away.

pandas Series built with dtype=object in this study's scoring wrapper. Upstream evaluate_sequences replaces a string cell with a list; pandas 0.25.3 (upstream's pin) had object dtype there, pandas 3 infers strict str and rejects it. The Series is constructed by this wrapper, not by upstream.
amendment_2.not_a_behaviour_change: None of the three alters a threshold, a hyperparameter, an architecture, the anomaly scoring, or the metrics. Each is a library-version incompatibility in a 2018 artifact, and each is applied identically to both arms so it cannot favour either.
